To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the AMPA receptors in the spinal cord dorsal horn are changed in inflammatory hyperalgesia and that the change is associated with the increase in the number of CGRP-positive primary afferents.
the AMPA receptor subunits GluA2 and GluA3 are upregulated at the synapse between CGRP-expressing primary afferent nociceptive fibers and dorsal horn neurons during inflammatory hyperalgesia.

the expression and function of GluR2-lacking AMPA receptors in spinal nociceptive synapses are increased during inflammatory hyperalgesia, which is a result of the activation of protein kinase C (PKC) in the spinal dorsal horn.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the nervous system responds to pain and how the brain controls pain.
the role of the spinal dorsal horn in pain and analgesia, and how it is affected by inflammation and nerve injury.
the role of AMPA receptors in the spinal cord in nociceptive transmission.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AMPA receptor subunits GluR1 and GluR2, as well as the NR1 and NR2A NMDAR subunits, are involved in the development of hyperalgesia in the formalin test.
AMPA receptor subunit composition is altered in spinal cord synapses during inflammation, and that this change in receptor subunit composition may contribute to hyperalgesia.
the AMPA receptor GluA2 subunit is not essential for the maintenance of normal pain sensitivity, but is required for inflammatory hyperalgesia and allodynia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

AMPA receptors are involved in the development and expression of inflammatory hyperalgesia, and that the AMPA receptor subunit GluR2 is a key determinant of this process [1]  The AMPA subtype of glutamate receptors is the major mediator of excitatory neurotransmission at central synapses.

we have demonstrated that there are at least two types of nociceptive primary aferent fibers in the spinal cord: those that express neuregulin-1 and its receptor ErbB2/4, and those that do not express these proteins.
AMPA receptors in nociceptive synapses are changed during inflammatory hyperalgesia, and this may contribute to the development of inflammatory pain.

there is no single type of pain.
